idiom_name: cppkafka::MessageBuilder headers over rdkafka header support
implementation_notes: cppkafka exposes Kafka record headers (rdkafka >= 0.11.4 required), so the history is one header key whose value is the serialized hop list: on receive, decode the incoming list, append this component's entry, re-encode, and produce a new record with the accumulated history. The classic structure is replaced by the C++ broker client's header container plus a small encode/decode pair; the append itself is your code, since the library only carries the bytes. Bound the list before producing: Kafka enforces a maximum record size including headers.
pitfalls: Header values are byte buffers: the entry format (JSON, CSV, length-prefixed) must be agreed and versioned, and a missing decode turns the value into an opaque blob on the next hop.
librdkafka header objects are copies: republishing a record without copying its incoming headers silently drops the accumulated history.
The producer is asynchronous - the history you pass is copied into the internal queue, but the payload you own must stay alive until the delivery callback fires.

variants.name: MQTT v5 user properties via Eclipse Paho C++
variants.idiom_name: mqtt::properties with one USER_PROPERTY per hop
variants.implementation_notes: Paho C++ (C++17) supports MQTT v5, whose PUBLISH packet carries user properties: one USER_PROPERTY whose value is the serialized hop list is the closest MQTT offers to a header field. Suited to edge and IoT hops where Kafka-sized records are not available; because MQTT properties are a flat name/value sequence and some hops may be MQTT 3.1.1, either keep a single value that you replace on each hop or refuse to route history through downlevel links.
pitfalls: User properties are unordered name/value pairs on the wire, so a reader cannot rely on position: index the entries in the value or keep the list in a single property.
An MQTT 3.1.1 hop has no properties at all and silently drops the trail - the history must tolerate a downlevel link or the flow must forbid one.
Paho callbacks run on the library's network thread: serializing or capping history there must not block, and a blocking call from inside the callback deadlocks.
